steps.text: Melt caramels with water in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat or in the microwave, stirring frequently. Remove from heat and cool to room temperature.
Beat cream cheese and sugar together in a medium bowl until fluffy; fold in caramel mixture. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Caramel Apple Dip
raw_recipe.description: This caramel apple dip is easy to make with soft caramels, brown sugar, and cream cheese for a delicious treat that's sure to become a fall favorite.
raw_recipe.name: Caramel Apple Dip

recipeInstructions.text: Melt caramels with water in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat or in the microwave, stirring frequently. Remove from heat and cool to room temperature.
Beat cream cheese and sugar together in a medium bowl until fluffy; fold in caramel mixture. Serve immediately.

review.reviewBody: This was definitely the hit of my party. I sliced all but 3 small apples of a 3 lb. bag and every apple was gone the the bowl licked clean. I was worried it was going to be too sweet but went ahead and added all the sugar anyway. It was perfect! I wanted to have all the food prep work done hours before the party so to keep the sliced apples from browning I put them in a bowl of about 4 cups of water and 1/4 cup lemon juice and kept them in the fridge. Right before I was ready to serve them I drained them and served them on a large platter with the dip in the middle. The last apple was as white as when I first served it.

I absolutely loved this recipe. I found the Kraft Caramel Bits which is wonderful. No unwrapping caramels forever. For those using these I called Kraft and was told 1 cups of bits = 25 caramels. When I added just 1 cup of the caramel bits it was very watery. I feared it would not firm up so since I love caramel anyway I added the whole bag. I put it in the fridge since we wasn't eating until the next couple days. It is a little thick but still good consistency for dipping. I love this dip!! The cream cheese gave it a richer taste. It certainly was hit!!

This recipe definitely deserves a review! Per the suggestions of previous reviewers, I increased the caramel to 24 pieces, which was perfect! The caramels took a while to melt on my stove, but the finished product was worth the wait! This was the last dish I prepared, based on the suggestion to serve immediately. However, it held up really well. I also soaked apple slices in salt water, before rinsing and refrigerating, so they too held up. Guests were still snacking on it over after dinner drinks. This is definitely a "keeper" and will become a "go to" for fall!

I added a splash of vanilla and didn't bother with folding in the caramel - just used a handmixer to whip it together. Next time I'll add a bit less water to the caramels that is recommended and might add some cinnamon or nutmeg for a bit of spice. Sinful as one friend described it!

So, I made this because I had some creamy caramel dip left over (from aldi - you get in produce section near caramel apples.) I used 2/3 of a cup of the dip and 1/2 t vanilla with the cream cheese & brown sugar. It's delish! Normally I don't alter a recipe the first time I try it, but just thought I'd share in case anyone was looking for a short cut or also had leftover caramel dip to use up! Serving with apples, grapes and cinnamon graham cracker sticks at a shower.

I make this a little different. I use confectionary sugar - 2 pksg. of cream cheese and concode caramel dip - ( found in the produce section) I use an electric mixer for the cream cheese, layer it on the bottom, warm the caramel in the microwave and spread it on top and use green apples to dip. It is always a crowd pleaser! You can cut the apples a head of time , put in a zip lock bag with a little orange juice so they don't brown.

To make this even easier, instead of melting caramels, I put a layer of caramel ice cream topping on top of the cream cheese mixture (don't fold in) and then as an added bonus I sprinkle crushed skor bar on top.

Outrageously delicious!!! Took advice to add a little vanilla and a few extra caramels. Melted the caramels in the microwave, added to the cream cheese mixture, and it turned out wonderful! Definitely a "keeper".
I doubled the caramels and followed the rest of the recipe. I put in blender to make it s-m-o-o-t-h. I could just eat it with a spoon. Sooooo GOOD !!!

I just tried this recipe last night, and it was great! I am so excited to bring it to thanksgiving! I mostly followed the recipe, accept I melted the caramels and water together in the microwave, stirring about every 20 seconds until smooth, and I added about 1/4 teaspoon of vanilla extract. My husband started stealing it before I could put it in the container! Very good!!

This was very good! I did make a few changes because I was making it for children who do not like cream cheese very well. I used a whole bag of caramel, 3/4 of low fat cream cheese, and added a bit of milk to the water to melt the caramel. The kids loved it and so did the adults!! Oh also added 1 tsp vanilla like other reviewers. Yum!
This was an easy recipe to follow. I cut the sugar and cream cheese in half. I added a tsp of vanilla. Thanks for the recipe idea.

I give it a 5 star rating because it is genius and tastes great. The initial flavor is spot on for carmel apples, but I found as the taste lingers the sourness of the cream cheese came thru too strong. As other reviewers mentioned, I’ll up the carmel and add a little vanilla. The microwave option was awesome.
Absolutely DELICIOUS! This caramel dip was the hit of the party! Will make this again and again!
Absolutely DELICIOUS! This caramel dip was the hit of the party! Will make this again and again!
I added vanilla and peanut butter. It was best dip ever with my apples.
Love this recipe! I sprinkle Health English Toffee Bits on the top of the dip when I serve it, adds a crunch and guests love it!!
